answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to a unique basalt pillar of admission proof, a single-use token that can never be split or reused. Every new agent enters through the same public harbor, where its behavior record is stamped with a fixed origin marker. Reputation then grows across the meadow of attested history, layering trust gradually. Because cloning demands a fresh basalt pillar per fake identity, and the harbor registry exposes clustered origins, a sybil swarm pays a steep per-clone cost in compute and detection risk.
